name: Primatial Cathedral of Bogotá
scope: Extant Primatial Cathedral of Bogotá with its current twin belfries, restored pediment, plaza steps, long tiled roofs and mapped secondary wings.
era: Extant neoclassical cathedral after rebuilding the upper facade and towers in the twentieth century

originalReview.notes: The 1846 public-domain watercolor is used for the lower west facade’s three plain rectangular doors, raised steps, lower pilaster rhythm and relationship to the plaza. Its pre-restoration upper stages and setting are not used for the current geometry.

The named photographer’s released original shows the extant west upper composition, both square belfry stages with large round arches, octagonal curved domes and lanterns, stone pilaster rhythm, broad cornices, the pediment and curved links to the bell towers.

review.method: Published Qualla watercolor plus exact current self-released bell-tower photograph
review.notes: Reviewed the published Qualla image first. The exact 1846 watercolor is identified by the national bank’s art collection as AP0057, with the independently recorded 1895 death of the artist. It supplies the lower facade rhythm. The exact 2009 named self-release supplies the current upper stages. Attribution-only photos and unverified original releases were skipped.
